purpose: Learner-experience layer over Course Truth, Exam Truth and the Course Learning Blueprint. It chooses the engaging practice formats for each requirement, records specification-precision boundaries and synoptic links, and maps every format to the Practice activity modes the learner-asset builder already produces.

rights.content: Structured facts and Revision-authored descriptions only. No AQA specification, question or mark-scheme prose is reproduced as teaching copy. Named researchers and terms are listed because the specification requires them.

courseMixTargets.source: AQA 7182 v1.4 scheme of assessment (structured facts)
courseMixTargets.rule: Over a typical fortnight, a learner's practice should give at least these shares to evaluation (AO3), research methods and maths. Recall-only practice alone cannot meet the mix.

formats.name: Study Autopsy
formats.learnerDescription: Pull apart a short made-up study: what was measured, how, what went wrong and what would fix it.

formats.name: Apply It
formats.learnerDescription: A short real-life situation. Use the psychology to explain what is happening, using the cues given.

formats.name: Evaluation Duel
formats.learnerDescription: Make a point, face the counterpoint, then land a judgement. Builds the evaluation that carries the most marks.

formats.name: Debate Link-up
formats.learnerDescription: Take one big debate and connect it to topics from across the course, with a reason for each link.

formats.name: Number Sprint
formats.learnerDescription: Quick timed calculations, each followed by a one-line 'so what does that show?'.

formats.name: Read the Data
formats.learnerDescription: A table, graph or result to interpret: spot the pattern, the limit and the conclusion you can and cannot draw.

formats.name: Test Picker
formats.learnerDescription: Given a study, choose the right statistical test and justify it from the design and level of data.

formats.name: Study Cards
formats.learnerDescription: Fast recall of the named researchers and studies: what they did, what they found, one strength, one weakness.

formats.name: Sort It
formats.learnerDescription: Drag items into the right group or order: symptoms by type, stages in sequence, features by store.

formats.name: Myth Buster
formats.learnerDescription: Spot the common wrong idea and say why it is wrong.

formats.name: Explain Chain
formats.learnerDescription: Build the mechanism step by step: this happens, which causes that, which leads to this.

formats.name: The Clinic
formats.learnerDescription: You are the practitioner. Read the case, choose a treatment or intervention and justify it against the alternative.

formats.name: Design It
formats.learnerDescription: Plan a small piece of research for a given aim: hypothesis, design, sample, controls, ethics.

formats.name: Essay Builder
formats.learnerDescription: Build a 16-mark answer in pieces: knowledge paragraph, application, then evaluation, with the support fading each time.

requirements.specificationBoundary: Types of conformity named in v1.4 are internalisation and compliance only. Explanations: informational and normative social influence.
requirements.scenarioHook: Everyone in the group chat says the answer to Q3 is B. You are fairly sure it is C.

requirements.specificationBoundary: Situational variables named: proximity, location and uniform. The dispositional explanation named is the Authoritarian Personality.

One friend refuses to join in a prank at a party, and then two others refuse too.

requirements.specificationBoundary: v1.4 lists minority influence through consistency, commitment and flexibility. Social change is not listed as a separate point.
requirements.scenarioHook: Two students start a campaign to stop homework being set on Fridays.

requirements.specificationBoundary: Features of each store: coding, capacity and duration.

requirements.specificationBoundary: Three attachment types are named: secure, insecure-avoidant and insecure-resistant.
v1.4 calls these definitions in the field of mental health, with deviation from ideal mental health listed first.
Characteristics are split into behavioural, emotional and cognitive for each of the three disorders.

requirements.specificationBoundary: In v1.4, cognitive neuroscience sits under the biological approach, not the cognitive approach.
Defence mechanisms named: repression, denial and displacement.

requirements.scenarioHook: The thirty seconds before you walk on stage for a performance.

requirements.specificationBoundary: Students should be able to choose a method for a research aim and compare methods.
Students must distinguish correlations from experiments, including what each can and cannot show about cause.

namedInSpecification: abstract, introduction, method, results, discussion, referencing

requirements.specificationBoundary: Subject content names calculation of mean, median, mode, range and percentages. The maths annex also lists 'calculate standard deviation'. Practise interpreting standard deviation throughout; treat SD calculation as a point to confirm with AQA before setting it.

namedInSpecification: graphs, tables, scattergrams, bar charts, histograms
requirements.specificationBoundary: Students must be able to choose and sketch an appropriate display for a given data set.
Includes locating the mean, median and mode on normal and skewed distributions.
Interpret coefficients (direction and strength). Calculating Spearman's or Pearson's coefficient is not required.
The sign test is the only inferential test students must calculate in full.

namedInSpecification: Type I and Type II errors
requirements.specificationBoundary: Students use statistical tables and critical values to judge significance, including one- and two-tailed tests.
Choose the test from design and level of measurement. Full calculation is not required for these seven tests; the maths annex does expect simple steps such as degrees of freedom for Chi-Squared.

namedInSpecification: filter theory (social demography, similarity in attitudes, complementarity)
